state:
Goal `core-objectmap`. `Core\ObjectMap` has its class card, and `clear`, `count` and `get` have every feature proof: about, examples, attack, bench with a recorded figure, and a Novis and a Rust test each.
The `get` bench found that every identity-store lookup allocated its chain key on the heap. `crate::identity_store::ChainKey` now builds it on the stack, so `get` records 0 allocations; this also speeds up `Core\ObjectSet`, which shares the store.
The remaining members are `set`, `has`, `remove`, `isEmpty`, `keys`, `values` and the constructor. Their tests already exist: `the_two_stores_stay_paired_through_set_and_remove` in `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/objmap.rs` carries `covers:` for set/get/remove/count/keys/values, and the three `object-map-*` conformance cases name what they assert.

next.title: member proofs
next.note: Run `bun nv proofs --id '<member>'` first; a test may only owe a `covers:` line.

items.text: **`Core\ObjectMap::has`** — owes about, examples, hostile, perf, and probably a `covers:` on `tests/conformance/core/object-map-has-is-the-only-member-that-tells-an-absent-key-from-a-null-value.nvst` plus a Rust test. `rule:testing/feature-proofs`. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/objmap.rs:98`
**`Core\ObjectMap::isEmpty`** — owes about, examples, hostile, perf and a Rust test; the sweep case already names it. A bench declares `allocations 0`. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/objmap.rs:125`

**`Core\ObjectMap::set`** — owes about, examples, hostile, perf. Its bench will not reach `allocations 0` when it inserts a new key (a store entry is an allocation); re-`set` of a present key is the zero-allocation case to measure. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/objmap.rs:80`

backlog: `remove`, `keys`, `values` and the constructor follow the same shape — `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/objmap.rs`.
A bench that indexes an array with a `uint` pays 2 allocations per read; `benches/members/README.md` § *Index with an `int`* owns that.
`?uint ?? 0` types as `mixed` because the literal is an `int`; write `?? (0 as uint)` — not a bug this goal owns.
`nvs agent show 'Core\ObjectMap'` prints the member list but not the class card's text, and `Core\Net\Stream` does the same; not checked whether that is intended — `crates/nvs-cli` agent renderer.
